audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 fits 50.92% over 542 games, and matches the mirror audit's read: his levels 2-3, even middle, Gangplank's after Sheen.

audit.whatIsWrong: First item and 2+ items were both marked Rumble, contradicting whys[5] ('finally out-bursts a single Flamespitter rotation') and whys[6] ('you out-scale a melee AP bruiser... your late-game sidelane 1v1 wins').
audit.why: Rumble is a melee-leash AP bruiser with no dash; once chained kegs and a Sheen-empowered Parrrley exist he cannot reach Gangplank. The packet chart marks both stages Gangplank.
audit.corrected: First item = Gangplank 7/10, 2+ items = Gangplank 8/10. Levels 1-5 and 6 unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early text says 'if he overheats into the Danger Zone' — it conflates two different passive states, and it gets the consequence backwards. Scrap Shield is also presented as the bait-and-commit cooldown without noting it is only 6 seconds. 'Powder Kegs' plural persists from the mirror's finding.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: 'When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells.' Overheat is the window where he CANNOT cast — it is Gangplank's opening, not a threat to flee. And a 6-second shield is not something you bait a commit around; telling the player to wait for it wastes the actual window.
audit.corrected: Danger Zone (50% Heat, empowered abilities) and Overheat (100% Heat, no casts) separated and the Overheat lockout named as the step-up window; Scrap Shield given its 6s so the player stops waiting on it; Flamespitter given 600 range / 10s; Powder Keg singular.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry warns that The Equalizer can be laid across the retreat path rather than on top of you.
audit.why: R is 1750 range, 130s at rank 1, and creates a slowing wall of flame. Gangplank has no dash, so Flash is the only out and it has to be held for the wall, not spent on the damage.
audit.corrected: Added to the late text and the don'ts.

edits.after: - Rumble Scrap Shield (6s): it is back fast — the real window is Overheat, when he cannot cast at all. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.after: Rumble's Flamespitter (Q, 10s) out-DPSes your autos in melee and free-hits your Powder Keg (E) before a chain exists, so he wins point-blank trades and denies your keg setup.

edits.before: Rumble's Flamespitter (Q) is the early-game problem. It out-DPSes your autos point-blank and free-hits your Powder Kegs (E) before they can chain, so don't place barrels where his cone can pop them. Farm with the tip of Parrrley (Q) and stay out of Flamespitter range entirely; if he overheats into the Danger Zone his Q burn and the bonus damage will shred you. Never trade autos into a heated Rumble at levels 1-3 - your durability loses that exchange.
edits.after: Rumble's Flamespitter (Q, 600 range, 10s) is the early-game problem. It out-DPSes your autos point-blank and free-hits your Powder Keg before it can chain, so don't place barrels where his cone can pop them. Farm with the tip of Parrrley and stay out of the cone: at 50% Heat he enters Danger Zone and every ability is empowered. At 100% he Overheats and cannot cast at all — that lockout, not his shield, is when you step up.

edits.before: Free-hit your low-HP barrels with Flamespitter (Q) before they can chain, then overheat for the Danger Zone burst
edits.after: Free-hit your low-HP Powder Keg with Flamespitter (Q), then hit Danger Zone at 50% Heat for the empowered burst

edits.before: Land Electro Harpoon (E) to slow and stick you in Flamespitter range during his heated window
edits.after: Land both Electro Harpoon charges to slow you, shred your MR, and stick you in the Flamespitter cone

edits.before: Once your Sheen and keg build come together you flip this lane and own the scaling. Chained Powder Keg detonations and global Cannon Barrage (R) outrange everything Rumble has, and he's a melee-range AP bruiser who must walk into your barrels to deal damage. He's not a hard scaler like Vladimir or Kassadin, so your sidelane 1v1 wins outright - just never get caught standing in his Equalizer during a fight, where his AoE burn and the slow lock you in.
edits.after: Once your Sheen and keg build come together you flip this lane and own the scaling. Chained Powder Keg detonations and global Cannon Barrage (R) outrange everything Rumble has, and he's a melee-range AP bruiser who must walk into your barrels to deal damage. He's not a hard scaler, so your sidelane 1v1 wins outright — just never get caught behind The Equalizer (130s, 1750 range): he can lay it across your retreat, and with no dash your only out is Flash.

notes: Main fix is the passive: the page said 'if he overheats into the Danger Zone', merging two opposite states. Danger Zone at 50% Heat empowers his abilities; Overheat at 100% locks him out of casting entirely and is Gangplank's step-up window. Also flagged that Scrap Shield — the ability this whole entry is built around tracking — is a 6-second cooldown, so 'bait it then commit' was never a real window. Rumble's W carries a 'terrain' derived flag that contradicts Riot's description (a shield and a speed burst); I did not use it, only the R for the retreat-cutting point.
